newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BEAZLEY WORRIED FOR LAWRENCE
Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says he's worried for Carmen Lawrence, who has been charged with perjury in relation to her evidence to the Easton Royal Commission in 1995.
Dr Lawrence has stood down from the Opposition front-bench and Shadow Immigration Minister, Duncan Kerr, will take over her Environment portfolio.
Mr Beazley told reporters in Adelaide that Dr Lawrence was very upset by the news of the charges, and he too was extremely sad and upset.
But he says he's not somebody who gives up friends lightly. He says he does not expect the government to pay her legal costs.
WA ACTING PREMIER HAS NO SYMPATHY FOR CARMEN
Western Australia's Acting Premier, Hendy Cowan says he doesn't think the State Cabinet would agree to help former Premier Carmen Lawrence defend perjury charges.
Dr Lawrence has been charged with with three counts of perjury, arising from evidence she gave to the Easton Royal Commission in 1995.
Mr Cowan has told commercial radio in Perth he does not feel sorry for Dr Lawrence.
State MP John Halden and Dr Lawrence's former senior advisor Ed Russell, have also been charged with perjury in relation to the same matter.
Dr Lawrence and Mr Halden will appear in court on Thursday. In W.A., the charge of perjury carries a maximum penalty of 14 years jail.
NO EVIDENCE THAT ABORIGINES WERE CANNIBALS-HISTORIAN
A North Queensland historian says there's no evidence to back up claims in the book "Pauline Hanson, The Truth" that Aborigines in the region were once cannibals.
Doctor Henry Reynolds from James Cook University says Europeans believed Aborigines were cannibals in the nineteenth century and accounts of cannibalism were common in newspapers of the time.
But, Doctor Reynolds says, when the accounts are looked at objectively they do not stand up.
He says the claims in the new book are extraordinary and not well researched.
INDUSTRY WELCOMES VIC GOVT CRACKDOWN ON BACKYARD OPERATORS
Industry groups have welcomed the Victorian Government's plan to crack down on the state's backyard meat industry.

The Victorian Government says backyard processors and unregistered meat trucks are threatening the reputation of Victoria's food industry and plans to combat them with fines, inspections and vehicle seizures.
The National Meat Association says it's delighted the Victorian government will introduce the legislation.
President David Abba says it will help the industry keep tabs on operators at the bottom end of the market.
The Victorian Meat Authority says its thrilled with the Government's approach and believes the legislation will dramatically improve compliance.
Chairman, John Watson, says those at the bottom end of the market have been giving the rest of the industry a bad name.
POWERFUL BACKING FOR MELBOURNE-DARWIN RAIL PLAN-MINISTER
The Northern Territory Transport Minister says the consortium proposing to build a railway from Melbourne to Darwin has obviously been able to stick its foot in the Prime Minister's door.
Barry Coulter says the proposed Adelaide to Darwin rail link is much further advanced than the alternative proposal to build a railway from Melbourne to Darwin via Queensland.
But, Mr Coulter says the consortium promoting the alternative plan is fairly powerful and has some political heavyweights on board.
He says the Adelaide to Darwin project is almost ready to go to the market place, after a decade of work.
NEW PARK FOR CENTRAL SYDNEY
Sydney Lord Mayor Frank Sartor, says a new park to be created in the middle of the city will be a boon for central business district residents.
Sydney City Council last night approved the merger of Phillip and Cook Parks in the city's east, creating a new four hectare facility.
The 30-million dollar project will include a new aquatic centre and a plaza outside Saint Marys Cathedral.
Councillor Sartor has told ABC Radio the park will be finished by 1999.
GREENPEACE FEARS FOR GREEN OLYMPICS
Greenpeace is accusing the New South Wales government of moving to abandon its commitment to a "green" Olympic Games.
Protestors are at the International Rowing Pavillion at Penrith in Sydney's west, claiming there are secret plans to use new turpentine timber, not recycled timber, as promised.
Greenpeace says it's another betrayal of the government's pledge to stage a "green" Olympic Games.
Spokesman Darren Gladman says Abigroup, the company building the Pavillion, must be forced to live up to its promise.
